text: The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 95 megawatts, according to a planning memorandum cited by the Ministry of Marine Energy on Tuesday. The document, circulated to regional officials on 14 October, says the facility’s first two turbine strings will provide 62 megawatts, with a third array bringing the installed capacity to the full figure. A ministry spokesman, Ivar Noll, said the rating reflects average output under standard spring-tide conditions and not the plant’s peak surge potential. The memorandum also notes that the project, built by Northgate Hydro Systems, is expected to supply power to about 48,000 homes across the Keld Strait grid once commercial operations begin next spring.
